::: {#rem-hardness-amplification}
#### Hardness amplification

A Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^\ell \to \{0,1\}$
is determined by its *truth table*, a binary string of length $2^\ell$,
so it can be encoded like any message.
Encode the truth table with a locally decodable code,
and read the codeword as the truth table of a new function $\hat f$.
If a small circuit computed $\hat f$ correctly on most inputs,
then running a local decoder on that circuit's outputs
would compute $f$ correctly on every input, with high probability,
using a circuit not much larger.
So if no small circuit computes $f$ on every input,
then no small circuit computes $\hat f$ on most inputs.
@arora2009computational [chapter 19] develop this worst-case to average-case
hardness amplification,
and their chapter 20 uses it to build pseudorandom generators.

:::
